questions.q: Which body grants formal approval for a high-impact change?
questions.explain: The CAB brings together stakeholders and arbitrates risk before production deployment.

questions.q: A patch fails immediately after deployment. What decision is expected first?
options: Wait for the next CAB meeting
Execute the backout plan during the maintenance window
Completely reinstall the system without a backup
questions.explain: Backout planning allows returning to a known-good state; it must be executable within the scheduled window.

questions.q: Which elements must be analyzed before approving a change? (Select all that apply)
options: Effect on allow/deny lists and security controls
The color of the ticket in the tool
questions.explain: Impact analysis covers availability, dependencies, and security, and relies on documented test results.

questions.q: When rolling back is impossible because data has already been migrated, which strategy is appropriate?
questions.explain: Fail forward involves moving ahead with a hotfix or workaround when rolling back is riskier.

questions.q: Which action is part of closing a change request?
questions.explain: Diagrams, policies/procedures, and version control must reflect the actual post-change state.

questions.q: What risk is specifically associated with legacy applications in a change analysis?
options: They depend on older protocols or ports that a change might remove
questions.explain: An unsupported application is often the only component still relying on a legacy protocol or port, making it a critical dependency.
